extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal education funds (elementary, secondary, and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, and compliance/legal staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how recipients must conduct Title IX grievance procedures, notify parties, provide remedies and supportive measures, handle disciplinary sanctions, and address false statements and consensual sexual activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notification of determination whether sex discrimination occurred (§106.45(h)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide written notification to the complainant and respondent of the determination whether sex discrimination occurred under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must be in writing and include the rationale for the determination and the procedures and permissible bases for the complainant and respondent to appeal, if applicable. Recipients have flexibility on the level of detail to include. Notices must be provided in adaptive formats as necessary to accommodate a student's disability and must comply with IDEA and/or Section 504 when applicable. Elementary and secondary schools are not subject to the Clery Act but are nevertheless required to provide written determinations under this provision. Recipients already maintain documentation under §106.8(f)(1), so written notice should not impose significant additional burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator role: coordinate provision and implementation of remedies (§106.45(h)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator must coordinate the provision and implementation of remedies following a determination that sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient is ultimately responsible for compliance; the Title IX Coordinator may delegate duties (§106.8(a)(2)). The Coordinator coordinates, rather than unilaterally provides, remedies (e.g., transcript changes coordinated with registrar; counseling through counseling office). Remedies may only be provided after a determination that sex discrimination occurred; discipline cannot be imposed absent such a determination. The recipient must ensure remedies are designed to restore or preserve access to its education program or activity (see definition of 'remedies' §106.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide remedies to complainant and other persons when appropriate (§106.45(h)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may provide remedies not only to the complainant but also to other persons identified by the recipient as having had equal access limited or denied by sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation changed 'or other person' to 'and other persons' to recognize circumstances where multiple individuals were affected (example: other girls in a robotics club subject to the same hostile environment). Remedies may include actions directed at others (training, schedule changes) and need not always require notifying the respondent if the remedy requires no action by respondent. However, if a remedy requires action by the respondent (e.g., changing a grade), the respondent would be notified. Remedies for graduates may be limited but recipients can still implement some measures (e.g., restrict respondent's access to alumni events).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify complainant of disciplinary sanctions imposed on respondent (§106.45(h)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: When disciplinary sanctions are imposed on a respondent following a determination that sex discrimination occurred, the Title IX Coordinator must notify the complainant of those sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification is required because knowledge of sanctions may impact the complainant's equal access to the education program or activity and may be necessary to prevent recurrence. The recipient coordinates implementation of disciplinary sanctions through the Coordinator or designees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may offer supportive measures regardless of a determination (§106.45(h)(3) and §106.44(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may offer supportive measures even if it does not determine that sex discrimination occurred, provided the measures do not unreasonably burden a party and are non-punitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures are designed to protect safety or access and to support parties during grievance procedures or informal resolution (§106.44(g)). They may not be provided for punitive or disciplinary reasons because a determination has not yet been made. Supportive measures can include schedule changes, no-contact orders, etc., so long as they don't unreasonably burden either party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with grievance procedures before imposing disciplinary sanctions (§106.45(h)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must follow the grievance procedures in §106.45 before imposing any disciplinary sanctions or other actions that are not supportive measures against a respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies to all complaints of sex discrimination (not only formal sexual harassment complaints) and is intended to ensure an equitable, bias-free process. It balances expediency and due process; recipients retain discretion over sanctions and are not required to impose particular sanctions. State laws that require disciplinary action within certain timeframes should be followed unless they conflict with these regulations (§106.6(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to use non-disciplinary actions pre-determination: emergency removal, administrative leave, and supportive measures (§106.44(g)-(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may take certain non-disciplinary actions prior to a final determination to protect safety or access, including supportive measures, emergency removal of a respondent from an education program or activity, and administrative leave for employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must not unreasonably burden either party and must be non-punitive. Emergency removal (§106.44(h)) requires an individualized safety and risk analysis, a determination that an imminent and serious threat exists, and notice plus an opportunity to challenge immediately following removal. Administrative leave for employees is allowed under §106.44(i). Disciplinary sanctions, however, may only be imposed after a finding that sex discrimination occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on disciplining based solely on the determination whether sex discrimination occurred (§106.45(h)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not discipline parties, witnesses, or others 'based solely' on the recipient's determination whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision protects participation in grievance procedures by preventing the outcome alone from being the basis for discipline alleging false statements. Recipients may still discipline for materially false statements made in bad faith or initiate code-of-conduct processes where there is evidence independent of the Title IX determination; evidence developed during the Title IX process can be used in such disciplinary proceedings. The provision applies equally to all participants and does not prevent considering credibility during factfinding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interplay with retaliation protections (§106.71) when initiating disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Threatening or instituting disciplinary proceedings against someone who participated in a grievance procedure could constitute retaliation under §106.71, depending on the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must consider §106.71 when deciding whether to pursue disciplinary actions related to participation in grievance procedures. Section §106.45(h)(5) signals that discipline based solely on the Title IX outcome could be impermissible and potentially retaliatory; recipients retain discretion to discipline where independent evidence supports the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against punishing consensual sexual activity related to reporting (§106.45(h)(5) discussion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule addresses concerns that survivors have been punished for consensual sexual conduct and that such punishment chills reporting; commenters supported protecting reporters from discipline for consensual sexual conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes that some recipients have codes of conduct that prohibit consensual sexual conduct and that §106.45(h)(5) was supported by commenters because it can prevent disciplining individuals (including survivors) in ways that interfere with access to education or deter reporting. The Department considered comments but did not adopt additional separate requirements on institutional codes of conduct in this rulemaking; implementation will depend on recipient policies consistent with §106.45(h)(5).
